title: SkyLoreScriber
description: What the agent did, what it cost, and what anyone thought of it. Panels read runs and verdicts directly; the $source variable separates live chat from seeded rows and from evaluation sweeps.

list.name: source
list.label: Traffic
list.description: Live questions, seeded rows, or gold-set sweeps. The evaluation panels at the bottom always read 'eval' and ignore this.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS runs
FROM runs
WHERE source IN ($source) AND $__timeFilter(ts)

panels.title: Cost
panels.description: Summed over the selected range. NULL where genai-prices did not know the model -- an unpriced run is not a free one, so it is left out rather than counted as zero.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT sum(cost) AS cost
FROM runs
WHERE source IN ($source) AND $__timeFilter(ts)

SELECT percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY seconds) AS p95
FROM runs
WHERE source IN ($source) AND $__timeFilter(ts)

panels.title: User feedback
panels.description: The only signal here that knows what the person actually wanted. Everything else on this dashboard is derivable without them.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE v.score > 0) AS "thumbs up",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE v.score < 0) AS "thumbs down"
FROM verdicts v JOIN runs r ON r.id = v.run_id
WHERE v.source = 'user' AND r.source IN ($source) AND $__timeFilter(v.ts)

panels.title: Trajectory checks, pass rate
panels.description: Read off the tool calls on every run, with no model asked and nothing spent. language_carried: did the model pass the user's language to every corpus tool. used_the_corpus: did it ask the corpus at all before answering.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT v.evaluator,
       round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE v.passed) / nullif(count(*), 0), 1) AS pass_rate
FROM verdicts v JOIN runs r ON r.id = v.run_id
WHERE v.source = 'trajectory' AND r.source IN ($source) AND $__timeFilter(v.ts)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

SELECT $__timeGroup(ts, $__interval) AS time,
       source AS metric,
       count(*) AS runs
FROM runs
WHERE source IN ($source) AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Latency
panels.description: Wall time around the whole agent run -- every model request and every tool call -- because that is what the person waiting experiences.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroup(ts, $__interval) AS time,
       percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY seconds) AS p50,
       percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY seconds) AS p95
FROM runs
WHERE source IN ($source) AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

SELECT $__timeGroup(ts, $__interval) AS time,
       sum(cost) AS cost
FROM runs
WHERE source IN ($source) AND cost IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Tokens
panels.description: Input dominates by an order of magnitude: the corpus payloads are what the model reads, and one whole article is 25k tokens on its own.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroup(ts, $__interval) AS time,
       sum(input_tokens)  AS input,
       sum(output_tokens) AS output
FROM runs
WHERE source IN ($source) AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Tools called
panels.description: Which of the six the agent actually reaches for. A question the reference monitoring stack cannot ask, because it records model calls rather than runs.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT tool, count(*) AS calls
FROM runs r, unnest(r.tools) AS tool
WHERE r.source IN ($source) AND $__timeFilter(r.ts)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Recent runs

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time, lang, question,
       array_to_string(tools, ', ') AS tools,
       internet AS web,
       round(seconds::numeric, 1) AS seconds,
       round(cost::numeric, 4) AS cost
FROM runs
WHERE source IN ($source) AND $__timeFilter(ts)
ORDER BY ts DESC
LIMIT 20

panels.description: `web` says the web-search tool was offered for that question, not that it was used -- `tools` says that. An answer where the web was available and the model stayed in the corpus is the interesting one.

panels.title: Evaluation — the gold set, judged by a model
Judge, pass rate by rubric
panels.description: From `python -m scripts.evaluate_agent --record`. grounding: did the answer contain what that gold question requires. prose_contract: did it credit its cultures, keep native names as names, and declare a fallback as a fallback. Ignores the $source variable -- these only exist for eval runs.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT v.evaluator,
       round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE v.passed) / nullif(count(*), 0), 1) AS pass_rate
FROM verdicts v
WHERE v.source = 'judge' AND $__timeFilter(v.ts)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: What the judge failed, and why
panels.description: The reason column is the whole value of an LLM judge over a pass rate: a percentage says something is wrong, this says what.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT v.ts AS time, r.case_id, r.lang, v.evaluator, v.reason, v.model
FROM verdicts v JOIN runs r ON r.id = v.run_id
WHERE v.source = 'judge' AND v.passed IS FALSE AND $__timeFilter(v.ts)
ORDER BY v.ts DESC
LIMIT 20
